system.summary: Four separate keys, each a homophonic substitution on graphic signs (two to seven homophones for common letters) with doubled-letter signs, a few nulls and a handful of code signs for persons (Mâcon's as numerals 20/30/40).
system.doubled_letters: special sign (LL, RR, SS, PP signs)
system.sibling_key: Lasry's 2023 tables (cryptiana GL.htm), each built from a sibling letter (fr. 3005 f. 107; fr. 3040 f. 16 / Clair. 330 f. 53; fr. 3019 f. 20; fr. 3053), plus Tomokiyo's partial tables; used as the key for all four.
system.notes: Digits occur only in the Mâcon key (codes 20, 30, 40). Code signs identified here: heart = roy and unlisted signs for Emperor, Florentines, Pope/Medici (1529); 8Δ = pape, key-ring = roy, ʃʃ-on-stem null (1530); 20/30/40 = Empereur/pape/roy (1537).

prior_solution.where: Keys published online by Lasry (tables dated 5 Nov 2023 on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm, with Tomokiyo's partial tables on francis.htm). Lasry also decoded all four texts in 2023, but those decipherments were never published (Lasry, 21 Sept 2026); 'partial' is the closest enum: the keys were public, the full reading existed but unpublished. A contemporary decipherment slip (f. 9bis) covers part of the Mâcon letter.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the catalogue item; no target-specific intervention recorded. Relayed Lasry's 21 Sept 2026 correction on his unpublished decipherments.
tools: Gallica image scripts (thumbs.py, full.py, crop.py, sheet.py)

solution.what: Matched the four items against Tomokiyo's francis.htm and GL.htm: four letters, four different keys, all tabulated by Lasry in 2023; no plaintext on either site.
Located the correct Gallica arks (fr. 3091 is btv1b9060253s, not the catalogue's) and fetched full-resolution canvases.
Transcribed the cipher of each letter at glyph level into ASCII aliases, page by page (per-page agents for the 171-line Gramont 1529 letter).
Applied Lasry's published tables to each letter (decode.py, macon_decode.py).
Read Langeac 1529 and Gramont 1529 in full, Gramont 1530 about 85 %, Mâcon 1537 about 90 % of the cipher; identified code signs left blank in the tables (heart, 8Δ, key-ring, 20/30/40) and a null.

The Mâcon slip f. 9bis, a contemporary decipherment of the f. 9v passage, matches the reading made first; Gramont 1529 dated by Clement VII's departure for Bologna and Orange before Florence, Gramont 1530 by the princes' return.

Correction from George Lasry: he decoded all four texts in 2023 when reconstructing the keys, but the decipherments were never published. Prior-solution record updated: a reading existed, unpublished, learned of after the reading and not used (only his keys were).

outcome.method_basis: All four letters were read with Lasry's 2023 key tables for these very letters on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm; no new cryptanalysis was needed.
outcome.notes: Langeac and Gramont 1529 read in full, Gramont 1530 ~85 %, Mâcon ~90 % of the cipher; no new cryptanalysis needed.
